// These tests change process CWD/backend selection and cannot run in parallel.
func TestCheckpointReplay_NonOverlappingUpdatesPreserved(t *testing.T) {
	a, b, remoteDir, cid, repoA, repoB, storeA, storeB := checkpointReplayFixture(t)
	ctx := t.Context()
	ref := mustRefName(t, cid)

	t.Chdir(a)
	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
	require.NoError(t, storeA.Write(ctx, checkpoint.SessionSummary{
		CheckpointID: cid, Summary: &checkpoint.Summary{Intent: "remote summary must survive"},
	}))
	require.NoError(t, pushCheckpointRefsAtTips(t, repoA, remoteDir, []plumbing.ReferenceName{ref}))

	t.Chdir(b)
	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
	require.NoError(t, storeB.Write(ctx, checkpoint.SessionTranscript{
		CheckpointID: cid, SessionID: "shared-session",
		Transcript: redact.AlreadyRedacted([]byte("{\"text\":\"local finalized transcript\"}\n")),
	}))
	queue, err := checkpoint.PushQueueForRepo(ctx, repoB)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, queue.EnqueueRef(repoB, ref))
	_, flushErr := flushCheckpointRefsQueue(ctx, repoB, pushSettings{remote: remoteDir})
	remaining, err := queue.Drain()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, flushErr)
	require.NotContains(t, remaining, ref)
	meta, err := storeB.ReadSessionMetadata(ctx, cid, 0)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	if meta.Summary == nil || meta.Summary.Intent != "remote summary must survive" {
		t.Errorf("successful recovery erased the other clone's summary; queue=%v, metadata=%+v", remaining, meta)
	}
	content, err := storeB.ReadSessionContent(ctx, cid, 0)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Contains(t, string(content.Transcript), "local finalized transcript")
}

func TestCheckpointReplay_ConflictingTranscriptUpdatesStayQueued(t *testing.T) {
	a, b, remoteDir, cid, repoA, repoB, storeA, storeB := checkpointReplayFixture(t)
	ctx := t.Context()
	ref := mustRefName(t, cid)
	writeTranscript := func(store checkpoint.PersistentStore, content string) {
		require.NoError(t, store.Write(ctx, checkpoint.SessionTranscript{
			CheckpointID: cid, SessionID: "shared-session",
			Transcript: redact.AlreadyRedacted([]byte(content)),
		}))
	}
	t.Chdir(a)
	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
	writeTranscript(storeA, "remote transcript\n")
	require.NoError(t, pushCheckpointRefsAtTips(t, repoA, remoteDir, []plumbing.ReferenceName{ref}))
	t.Chdir(b)
	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
	writeTranscript(storeB, "provisional local transcript\n")
	writeTranscript(storeB, "local transcript\n")
	localBefore, err := repoB.Reference(ref, true)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	remoteBefore := remoteRefHash(t, remoteDir, ref)
	queue, err := checkpoint.PushQueueForRepo(ctx, repoB)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, queue.EnqueueRef(repoB, ref))
	queuedBefore, err := queue.DrainEntries()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	pushed, flushErr := flushCheckpointRefsQueue(ctx, repoB, pushSettings{remote: remoteDir})
	require.ErrorIs(t, flushErr, checkpoint.ErrReplayConflict, "conflicting appends must not be reported as delivered")
	require.Zero(t, pushed)
	localAfter, err := repoB.Reference(ref, true)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, localBefore.Hash(), localAfter.Hash())
	require.Equal(t, remoteBefore, remoteRefHash(t, remoteDir, ref))
	queuedAfter, err := queue.DrainEntries()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, queuedBefore, queuedAfter, "retain the exact queued generation")
	localSession, err := storeB.ReadSessionContent(ctx, cid, 0)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, "local transcript\n", string(localSession.Transcript))
	t.Chdir(a)
	paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()
	remoteSession, err := storeA.ReadSessionContent(ctx, cid, 0)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, "remote transcript\n", string(remoteSession.Transcript))
}

func checkpointReplayFixtureFor(t *testing.T, backend string) (string, string, string, id.CheckpointID, *git.Repository, *git.Repository, checkpoint.PersistentStore, checkpoint.PersistentStore) {
	t.Helper()

// generateCheckpointSummary generates an AI summary for a checkpoint and persists it.
// The summary is generated from the scoped transcript (only this checkpoint's portion),
// not the entire session transcript.
//
// summaryTimeoutSeconds is the per-invocation --summary-timeout-seconds flag
// value (0 = unset). Effective precedence for the deadline: flag > settings >
// no deadline. See resolveSummaryTimeout for the resolution.
func generateCheckpointSummary(ctx context.Context, w, errW io.Writer, store checkpoint.Writer, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, cpSummary *checkpoint.CheckpointSummary, content *checkpoint.SessionContent, force bool, summaryTimeoutSeconds int) error {
	// Check if summary already exists
	if content.Metadata.Summary != nil && !force {
		return renderExplainFailure(errW, "Summary already exists", []explainRow{
			{Label: "id", Value: checkpointID.String()},
			{Label: explainLabelTry, Value: fmt.Sprintf("entire checkpoint explain --generate --force %s", checkpointID)},
		}, fmt.Errorf("checkpoint %s already has a summary", checkpointID))
	}

	// The summary is written back into the checkpoint, and compaction below
	// redacts what the provider sees, so both need the repo's rules.
	if err := strategy.EnsureRedactionConfigured(ctx); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("configure redaction: %w", err)
	}

	// Check if transcript exists
	if len(content.Transcript) == 0 {
		return renderExplainFailure(errW, "Checkpoint has no transcript", []explainRow{
			{Label: "id", Value: checkpointID.String()},
		}, fmt.Errorf("checkpoint %s has no transcript to summarize", checkpointID))
	}

	// Scope the transcript to only this checkpoint's portion
	scopedTranscript := scopeTranscriptForCheckpoint(content.Transcript, content.Metadata.GetTranscriptStart(), content.Metadata.Agent)
	if len(scopedTranscript) == 0 {
		return renderExplainFailure(errW, "Checkpoint has no transcript content (scoped)", []explainRow{
			{Label: "id", Value: checkpointID.String()},
		}, fmt.Errorf("checkpoint %s has no transcript content for this checkpoint (scoped)", checkpointID))
	}
	provider, err := resolveCheckpointSummaryProvider(ctx, w)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve summary provider: %w", err)
	}
	scopedTranscript = maybeCompactExternalTranscript(ctx, scopedTranscript, content.Metadata.Agent)

	// Generate summary using shared helper
	logging.Info(ctx, "generating checkpoint summary")
	if errW != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Generating checkpoint summary... (transcript: %s, provider: %s)\n",
			humanizeBytes(len(scopedTranscript)), provider.Name)
	}

	timeout := resolveSummaryTimeout(ctx, summaryTimeoutSeconds)

	attempt := newSummaryAttempt(provider.Name, timeout)
	// Set streaming eagerly from the provider's capability rather than waiting
	// for the first progress event: a streaming provider that stalls before
	// emitting anything should still get the streaming timeout diagnostic
	// ("never sent its request"), not "provider produced no output".
	attempt.streaming = provider.Streaming
	progressWriter := newSummaryProgressWriter(errW, attempt)

	start := time.Now()
	summary, err := generateCheckpointAISummary(
		ctx, scopedTranscript, cpSummary.FilesTouched,
		content.Metadata.Agent, provider.Generator,
		timeout, progressWriter.handle, attempt,
	)
	if err != nil {
		progressWriter.Flush()
		label, rows, structured := formatCheckpointSummaryError(err, attempt)
		styles := newStatusStyles(errW)
		fmt.Fprint(errW, styles.renderFailure(label, rows))
		return NewSilentError(structured)
	}
	elapsed := time.Since(start)

	if err := store.Write(ctx, checkpoint.SessionSummary{CheckpointID: checkpointID, Summary: summary}); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save summary: %w", err)
	}

	styles := newStatusStyles(w)
	rows := summaryProviderRows(provider)
	rows = append(rows, explainRow{Label: "duration", Value: formatSummaryDuration(elapsed)})
	fmt.Fprint(w, styles.renderSuccess(fmt.Sprintf("Summary generated for %s", checkpointID), rows))
	return nil
}

// formatSummaryDuration rounds wall-clock generation time to a human-friendly value.
func formatSummaryDuration(d time.Duration) string {
	return d.Round(100 * time.Millisecond).String()
}

func maybeCompactExternalTranscript(ctx context.Context, scopedTranscript []byte, agentType types.AgentType) []byte {
	if transcriptHasSummaryContent(scopedTranscript, agentType) {
		return scopedTranscript
	}

	ag, err := agent.GetByAgentType(agentType)
	if err != nil {
		external.DiscoverAndRegister(ctx)
		ag, err = agent.GetByAgentType(agentType)
	}
	if err != nil || !external.IsExternal(ag) {
		return scopedTranscript
	}

	compactor, ok := agent.AsTranscriptCompactor(ag)
	if !ok {
		return scopedTranscript
	}

	tmpFile, err := os.CreateTemp("", "entire-summary-transcript-*.jsonl")
	if err != nil {
		logging.Debug(ctx, "external summary compaction unavailable",
			slog.String("agent", string(agentType)),
			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
		return scopedTranscript
	}
	tmpPath := tmpFile.Name()
	defer func() {
		if removeErr := os.Remove(tmpPath); removeErr != nil {
			logging.Debug(ctx, "failed to remove temporary summary transcript",
				slog.String("path", tmpPath),
				slog.String("error", removeErr.Error()))
		}
	}()

	if _, err := tmpFile.Write(scopedTranscript); err != nil {
		_ = tmpFile.Close()
		logging.Debug(ctx, "external summary compaction transcript write failed",
			slog.String("agent", string(agentType)),
			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
		return scopedTranscript
	}
	if err := tmpFile.Close(); err != nil {
		logging.Debug(ctx, "external summary compaction transcript close failed",
			slog.String("agent", string(agentType)),
			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
		return scopedTranscript
	}

issues.title: fix(checkpoint): preserve concurrent sessions during replay
issues.body:
Closes #3014.

Two clones can append different sessions to the same numeric checkpoint slot. Recovery currently reports a successful push and clears the queue after replacing the remote clone's session. This merges sessions by ID so both additions reach the published checkpoint.

Ready for review. #3014 is newly filed and maintainer agreement on the approach is pending. The four full-suite failures below also reproduce on untouched current upstream; this PR does not claim a green full check.

## Reproduction

The standalone test in #3014 uses real checkpoint writers, the generation-aware queue and a local bare remote. I ran the same test against untouched `955fc9ede` and this implementation, with race detection:

| | Published session IDs | Push / queue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upstream `955fc9ede` | `shared-session`, `local-added-session` | Success; queue cleared |
| This PR | `shared-session`, `remote-added-session`, `local-added-session` | Success; queue cleared |

The remote's earlier commit remains an ancestor in both cases. The bug is missing content in the current checkpoint tree, rather than deletion of every older Git object. No live agent or hosted service is needed to reproduce it.

## Implementation

- Compare each replayed change against its original parent instead of blindly replacing tree entries. Incompatible changes stop before the recovered ref is installed and retain the queued generation.
- At checkpoint roots, match sessions by stable session ID. Keep remote order, append independent local sessions, update their file pointers and rebuild totals through the normal writer helpers. Retain the complete session trees, including transcripts, prompts and assets.
- Preserve independent metadata fields, unknown values, JSON number precision, file modes, review flags and commit links. The root branch label stays with the published checkpoint; each session keeps its own branch. Transcripts remain opaque blobs.
- Recognize an already-delivered linear commit sequence by its combined tree change. This lets a stale peer retain a finalized transcript while publishing new independent work.
- Exclude the intentionally deleted checkpoint from local replay during deletion reconciliation; keep unrelated work and the existing compare-and-swap rule.

The checkpoint schema and push-generation/CAS machinery are unchanged. The new merge code reuses the existing tree writer, subtree-removal, path validation, aggregation and JSON helpers.

## Review guide

`checkpoint/replay.go` handles tree-entry conflicts. `replay_sessions.go` handles session identity, paths and aggregates; `replay_json.go` handles metadata fields. `strategy/metadata_reconcile.go` connects replay and recognizes already-delivered sequences. The deletion caller supplies the existing subtree-removal helper.

The commits separate code/regression tests from the updated implementation contracts.

## Validation

- The original content-loss reproduction fails on current upstream and passes here.
- Regression coverage includes both `git-refs` and `git-branch`, connected/disconnected histories, backfills after reindexing, stale-peer retries, genuine conflicts, file modes, unknown fields, large integers, assets and queue retention.
- `mise run check` was run before each commit. Formatting/lint and the affected packages pass. The full run is not green: these four cases also fail on untouched upstream `955fc9ede` under the same environment:
  - `TestPromptCommitConfig_AbortIsReportedOnTheTerminal`
  - `TestManualCommit_MidSessionRebaseFollowsHead`
  - `TestCheckpointDelete_LeftoverDeletedIDNeverReceivesNewWork`
  - `TestOpenCodeSeedRepoPlantsDeps`
- Deterministic canaries pass on this branch: 53 Vogon and 4 Roger Roger scenarios. Cognitive complexity is checked against `upstream/main`.
- The second full check additionally hit `TestFetch_AbortStalledLetsProgressingFetchRun` once in an unchanged package. It passed 10 isolated runs on this branch and 10 on untouched upstream; the first full check passed that package. This is disclosed separately rather than counted among the four reproduced baseline failures.

Environment: macOS 14.7 arm64, Git 2.49.0, Go 1.27.3; Node 24.20.0 selected through a command-only override for broad checks. No paid real-agent E2E tests ran.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Action completed."}],"structuredContent":{"issues":[{"url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/3012","title":"Trail create: restore --checkout and --add-assignee; print the switch command","issue_number":3012,"body":"Project-trail `trail create` (the default since v0.12.0) dropped the legacy `--checkout` and `--add-assignee` flags, so scripts written for 0.9 fail with "unknown flag". And a create on the base branch publishes a new branch but leaves the local checkout on the base, stranding the work there (trail-review items 7 and 9).

- `--checkout`: after the trail is printed, switch to the published branch (git CLI). Uncommitted work carries over, since a derived branch starts at HEAD. If git refuses (an existing branch that conflicts), the command says the trail was created and gives `git switch <branch>`; `--json` stdout stays valid.
- Rejected with `--no-branch`, `--repo` and `--branch-action create`, since there's nothing local to switch to.

A `checkpoint_remote` that passes the ownership vote but has no URL the CLI can build fell back to the push remote. Pre-push then delivered session checkpoints to the code repository, possibly a public one, that the user had explicitly routed them away from. Today this hits any provider without a known host, e.g. `"provider": "entire"` with a github.com origin.

## Change

- `remote.PushURL` returns `ErrCheckpointRemoteUnroutable` (and no URL) instead of falling back to the push remote. The error says what to do: point `checkpoint_remote` at a github or gitlab repository, or remove it. It does not quote the remote URL; the parse cause is logged instead, so a URL's raw bytes never reach terminal output.
- A push remote whose URL does not parse (bare local path, scp-style URL with no owner) no longer falls back to origin either. The store is derived from origin's transport first, so a self-hosted origin keeps its checkpoints on its own host; otherwise it goes to the provider's host, or is withheld.
- Every push path honors the withhold, and the refs stay queued locally:
  - pre-push skips the checkpoint push and prints `[entire] Checkpoints were not pushed and stay local: …` on every push until the setting is fixed; the user's own `git push` is not blocked;
  - `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs` and the manual `PushCheckpoints` (`entire checkpoint push`) return the error;
  - `flushCheckpointRefs` refuses a withheld store itself, so a new caller cannot reopen the path.
- Read surfaces stop describing the push remote as the destination:
  - `CheckpointPushTarget` returns the error, so `attach` no longer reports "Pushed checkpoint metadata" for a checkpoint that went nowhere;
  - `status` reports checkpoints as not syncing;
  - remote topology treats the remote as pinned.

Unchanged: inherited (refused) stores still go to the push remote by design. Self-hosted origins still derive a URL on their own host for any provider. Reads are untouched.

## Notes

- Two existing tests pinned the old fallback and are flipped: a `TestPushURL` case (from 1238aff1e2, which fixed the same misroute for github/gitlab and left unknown providers on it), and `TestCheckpointClaimReport`'s unparseable-transport case, which now expects the dedicated store.
- `entire enable` now errors for such a config instead of passing silently.
- The withhold tests push to a reachable bare repository with a queued checkpoint ref and assert nothing lands there. Each was mutation-checked: reverting the `PushURL` fix delivers the ref and fails the test.
- Not covered: Git's own `push --all`/`--mirror`/explicit refspecs can still carry checkpoint refs in the outer push. That predates this change; main's `CheckOuterPushHeldCheckpoints` is the natural place to extend for a follow-up.
- `doctor migrate-checkpoints --remote <url>` still pushes to the URL given. That is the user naming the destination for one command, like an explicit `git push <url>`; the withhold covers the configured store.

This is step 1 toward supporting `entire` as a `checkpoint_remote` provider (Entire-native `entire://<cluster>/et/<project>/<repo>`). The remaining work (cluster resolution, flag/claim parsing, token handling, ownership vote) is out of scope here.

## Testing

Unit, integration and the Vogon canary pass locally, as do lint and `GOOS=windows go vet`. Two local-only exceptions: `TestOpenCodeSeedRepoPlantsDeps` fails with OpenCode 2 installed (CI doesn't run it), and `TestHTTPS_PushFailsWithoutToken/git-refs` hangs on this machine on the base commit too.

Part of trail #2688 (closing CLI trail command gaps), change cli/1735.

## What

Three read-only commands on one change, resolved like `trail approve`:

- `entire trail timeline [<trail>]` shows the change's activity newest first: commits (short SHA, title, +/- lines, agents), reviews posted, finding resolutions and dismissals, approvals, and lifecycle events. It pages 50 at a time; `--limit` and `--page-token` continue, and the next token is printed like `trail list` does.
- `entire trail sessions [<trail>]` lists the agent sessions behind the change's checkpoints (session ID, agent, model, start, checkpoint count, name).
- `entire trail stack [<trail>]` shows the pull request stack the change belongs to, bottom first, marking the current one; it says so when there is no stack.

All three read the cell's repository-ID routes. `--json` prints the server's response object unchanged for all three, so a new kind or field shows up in JSON without a CLI change, and the text view prints any unknown timeline kind with its time and actor. `--limit` is checked before the trail is resolved, so a bad value fails without authenticating. An empty timeline page says it is this page's, and still reports an incomplete load and the next page token.

## Not included

- The project-trail timeline (`/{host}/{project}/trails/{id}/timeline`) only carries trail-level edits (created, updated, change added), so it is not exposed here; the change timeline has the activity people ask about.
- Contributors: the cell only serves them as a base/head compare, and the timeline and `git log` already show who committed.

## Classification (intentional, please review)

`trail timeline`, `trail sessions`, and `trail stack` are classified `read-only` on purpose, and are not listed in the default agent-help view (`listed: false`). The repository default for new commands is user-owned, but these only issue GETs and change nothing, so they sit beside their read-only siblings `trail approvals` and `trail watch` in the trail block of `agentHelpClassification`. The sessions table does not print prompts; `--json` returns what the server sends, which includes each session's first prompt.

## Supporting changes

- `colHeaderModel` replaces the `"MODEL"` literal (also used twice in `project_agent_list.go`).
- `trailRepoIDNumberPath` moved out of the merge command into `trail_repo_id_path.go` with a neutral error, and `trailRepoIDPath` builds on it. That file and the legacy `RepoID` fix are identical to cli/1734's, so either PR can merge first without conflicts.

## Verification

- Tests cover every timeline kind's rendering (including an unknown kind), paging parameters and the next-token line, an empty page that is incomplete and has a next page, JSON pass-through with unknown fields for the timeline, sessions, and the stack, the `--limit` bounds failing before any request (mutation-checked), the sessions table and JSON, and both stack states, served in the server's real shape (`{"stack":null}` when there is none).
- Live against the production cell on cli/1731: `trail timeline` (and page 2 through the printed token), `trail sessions`, and `trail stack` all return the real data.
- `mise run fmt`, `mise run lint`, and `GOOS=windows go vet` are clean; `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... ./docs/...` passes. Locally, `TestHTTPS_PushFailsWithoutToken/git-refs` and `TestOpenCodeSeedRepoPlantsDeps` fail on an unmodified `main` checkout too, so the integration and e2e-agents packages were left to CI.

## What was wrong

If you commit from a worktree that has no Entire session, the CLI falls back to sessions from other worktrees of the same repo. `resolveWorktreeCandidates` only checks the 15-minute `recentSessionWindow` when those sessions come from more than one worktree. If they all come from one worktree, it links them without checking, no matter how long they've been idle. In the report, a Codex session that had been idle for over a day got linked to every commit made from another worktree. Each time, `post-commit` condensed its 5 GB transcript.

## The fix

`findSessionsForCommitLinking` now runs the fallback's matches through `withoutIdleSessions`. It drops a session whose last interaction is older than `recentSessionWindow`. These sessions are kept:

- a session with no recorded interaction, as before, because we don't know how long it's been idle;
- a session that's mid-turn (active phase, turn started within `activeSessionInteractionThreshold`), because `LastInteractionTime` only changes at turn boundaries;
- a session with a background subagent still running (`hasFreshLiveTaskRecord`), the same case `idleWithLiveTaskRecord` already trusts;
- a session that recorded edits in the committing worktree, which still joins through its worktree entry, limited to those edits.

Amend and post-rewrite use `findSessionsForWorktree` to keep existing links up to date, and they don't change. The multi-worktree path doesn't change either.

Here's how this differs from the patch in the issue. Review on my fork found that putting the check inside `resolveWorktreeCandidates` also hid idle sibling sessions from amend and post-rewrite. It also dropped sessions that were mid-turn or had a subagent running. So the check now runs only for commit linking, and it keeps those two cases. The drop is logged at Debug, without `idle_for`. I'm happy to switch to the Info line from your patch if you prefer it.

## What was wrong

`entire brain connect` moves the `pre-push` hook it finds to `pre-push.pre-entire-brain` and runs it through a path relative to its own:

```sh
backup="$0.pre-entire-brain"
if [ -x "$backup" ]; then exec "$backup" "$@"; fi
```

On uninstall, `restoreWrapped` only handles a moved copy that a wrapper names literally (`runsByName`). Brain's wrapper never names `pre-push.pre-entire-brain`, so `entire disable --uninstall` reported success but left Entire's hook in that file. The next `git push` still ran `entire hooks git pre-push`.

## The fix

- `isBrainChain` recognises only the exact wrapper entire-brain v0.4.0 writes, byte for byte except the single-quoted plugin path it bakes in. That wrapper exits 0 when its copy is gone. An earlier version of this fix parsed `"$0<suffix>"` references in any shell script. Five rounds of bot review on my fork each found another shell form it got wrong, so I switched to the exact match. Anything it doesn't accept, including an edited Brain wrapper, goes down the existing path, the same as on `main`.
- `restoreBrainChain` runs inside `restoreWrapped` when the moved copy holds Entire's hook:
  - Brain's wrapper in `pre-push`, no user hook in `pre-push.pre-entire`: the copy is removed.
  - Brain's wrapper in `pre-push`, a user hook in `pre-push.pre-entire`: the user's hook moves into the copy, where Brain's wrapper runs it. Brain's own install would have left it that way.
  - Entire's hook in `pre-push` and Brain's wrapper backed up (Entire re-wrapped Brain): the copy is removed before the wrapper is put back.
- Left as on `main`: a keep copy beside the moved file, and a user hook that names the copy or finds its own path (`$0`, `${0`, `BASH_SOURCE`, `__file__`, `sys.argv`, `__FILE__`, `__filename`, `__dirname`, `process.argv`), because moving such a hook could change what it runs.
- Install is unchanged.

## Why it needs #2959

With #2959, a later `entire enable` leaves a runnable Brain wrapper in front instead of re-wrapping it. The test case "Entire installed again after brain, with a user hook" expects exactly that: after uninstall, the user's hook still runs from behind Brain's wrapper, and Entire's doesn't. On `main` alone, the second install still re-wraps and rotates the user's hook away, so that case fails there (`pre-push.pre-entire-brain missing`, `ran "", want "user"`). The other cases pass both with and without #2959. "Entire re-wrapped a non-executable brain, user hook rotated away" covers the one path that still re-wraps (a wrapper that can't run).

If you'd rather fix it on the Brain side instead (giving Brain's wrapper a marker `doctor` recognizes), tell me and I'll close this.

## Why

`entire brain connect` installs its own `pre-push` hook. It moves the hook it finds (Entire's) to `pre-push.pre-entire-brain`, and its own hook ends with:

```sh
backup="$0.pre-entire-brain"
if [ -x "$backup" ]; then exec "$backup" "$@"; fi
```

So Entire's hook still runs, with git's stdin and arguments. But the new `pre-push` doesn't have the `# Entire CLI hooks` marker, so `hookStateIn` treats it as foreign and reports the whole set as `GitHooksAbsent`. I checked what happens next with the real plugin (brain v0.4.0, and v0.5.0 since its release today, see Verification):

- `entire doctor` shows `Git hooks: NOT INSTALLED` / "Commits in this repository are not captured as checkpoints" on a setup that works, and suggests `--force` to fix it.
- `EnsureSetup` runs on every agent turn and reinstalls whenever `IsGitHookInstalled` is false. On the first turn after `brain connect`, it backs Brain's hook up to `pre-push.pre-entire`, puts Entire's hook in front, and prints `[entire] Your pre-push hook still runs, after Entire's (moved to .git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire).` into the agent's hook output. After that, doctor says OK again.

Pushes keep working after that re-wrap. Entire's new `pre-push` runs Entire, then Brain's hook from `pre-push.pre-entire`. Brain's `$0`-relative chain then looks for `pre-push.pre-entire.pre-entire-brain`, which doesn't exist, so it stops there (Brain's source says that's deliberate, so the host's hook doesn't run twice). The old Entire copy in `pre-push.pre-entire-brain` is left behind and nothing runs it. So the bug users see is doctor's false report (and its `--force` advice) between …108082 chars truncated…ils on a line of 10 MiB or more, as on main, and the Pi agent package keeps its 10 MiB scanner. The adapter itself has no line limit, like Claude Code's: a long line is read whole and keeps its place in the tree, so the fold matches `Convert` wherever `Convert` succeeds. Lifting the checkpoint and `pijsonl` limits is left to a separate PR.

## Tests

The old `compactPi` is frozen as an oracle in `transcript/pi_oracle_test.go`. `transcript/pi_records_test.go` checks that folding the records equals the oracle and `Convert` after every line, with input fed a line at a time and in random 1–40-byte chunks. It also checks `Convert` against the oracle at every `StartLine`. It covers hand-written cases, fixtures, 1,000 generated trees, usage-only calls, images, CRLF and unterminated lines, lines over 10 MiB in the adapter, and `Convert` failing on them exactly where the old compactor did. `mise run check` passes.

Part of #2255. First of five stacked PRs that replace #2253.

Part of ENT-3643.

### Problem

Every reader of a saved commit scanned the whole message for `Entire-Checkpoint:`, so a line anywhere linked the commit: in the body, indented, pasted, or a teammate's trailer reused with `git commit -C`. Prepare-commit-msg took any such ID as its own stamp and added none, and post-commit then condensed the session's work into it. That created a checkpoint under a teammate's ID, or changed another commit's checkpoint.

### What changes

- **Only the last paragraph links a saved commit.** The `Entire-Checkpoint:` lines that start a line in the last non-subject paragraph count. Trailing blank and comment lines are skipped, and other lines in the paragraph are ignored. This is deliberately lenient; git's own trailer grammar comes in a later PR.
- **One resolver, `strategy.LinkedCheckpoints`, for code that writes into a checkpoint:** post-commit, attach and `explain --generate`.
  - It reads `core.commentChar`, `core.commentString` and `commit.cleanup` in one `git config` call, skipped when the message has no `Entire-Checkpoint` text.
  - Under `core.commentChar=auto` or a cleanup mode that keeps comment lines (`whitespace`, `verbatim`, `scissors`), it falls back to the whole-message scan, so no commit main links through a real trailer becomes unlinked.
  - Attach resolves once while planning and reuses the result.
- **Read-only views read without git config:** `explain <commit>`, `explain --commit`, the branch listing, `explain --checkpoint` search, export and the review re-run guard.
  - They read with `#` and show the last ID of the last paragraph, which is the one attach joins and `--generate` writes, or else the first ID anywhere.
  - For a squash commit they now show the checkpoint it stamped rather than the first inherited one.
- **Stamp record.**
  - Prepare records each ID it stamps in `entire-stamped-trailers.json` in the per-worktree git dir before writing the trailer: a generated one, a session's reservation, or one an amend restores. If it cannot record the ID, it writes no trailer.
  - An ID already in the draft counts as stamped only if the record holds it; otherwise prepare stamps a fresh trailer after it.
  - Post-commit consumes the record and condenses into the last stamped ID. Without one, it uses only the last ID whose checkpoint exists, for the session that owns it. It never creates a checkpoint prepare did not stamp.
- **Squash and redo inheritance** count only unindented trailers as already present. An editor squash, whose seeded message indents the squashed commits' trailers, now gets the inherited trailers in its last paragraph.
- **`explain --generate`** on a commit whose only ID is outside the last paragraph names that ID in its error.

Other read-only lookups (resume, status, attribution, other history listings) still scan the whole message.

### Known gaps

- In the fallback configurations, a body mention can still steer attach and `explain --generate`, and show in `explain`. A later PR applies git's real comment and cleanup rules and removes the fallback.
- `git commit -C`, `-c` and `--amend` keep a reused trailer and stamp none, so reusing a foreign one leaves the commit unlinked. `entire attach` can link it.
- The lenient reader accepts some last paragraphs git would not read as trailers, as main did. A later PR applies git's trailer grammar.
- When two commits race in one worktree, the first post-commit consumes the stamp record, so the second commit's trailer can end up without a checkpoint. The inherited-trailers marker has the same window.

### Tests

Each test was written first and seen failing before its fix.

- Trailer reader unit tests, resolver tests across git configurations, and stamp record and target selection unit tests.
- Attach and explain tests: body mentions do not select a checkpoint, and the listing and `--checkpoint` search agree with `explain <commit>`.
- Integration tests through the real hook binaries:
  - a body line naming an unknown checkpoint, and one naming an existing checkpoint;
  - an indented line;
  - an agent commit with a body line;
  - `git commit -C` of a commit naming an unfetched checkpoint;
  - a trailer replaced in the editor;
  - a last paragraph naming an unknown then an existing checkpoint.
- `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits` runs real `git commit` for `-m`, `-F`, editor, `--amend`, `--amend --no-edit`, `;` comments, `commit.cleanup` whitespace / verbatim / scissors, `core.commentChar=auto`, and `-F` of a message naming a foreign checkpoint. It asserts the commit stays linked and no foreign checkpoint is created.
- Post-commit fixtures that hand-write a trailer now record the stamp prepare would, or they return before the logic they pin.

Makes token accounting correct by construction. Today `entire` works out each checkpoint's tokens by slicing transcripts at offsets, and every double count and undercount we've found comes from those slices starting or ending in the wrong place: turns without file changes went missing (Claude Code `entire status` showed 64k against 285k actually spent), a repeated Stop on a turn that changed files counts the turn twice, a message whose lines straddle an agent's mid-turn commit counts twice, and Copilot counts cache twice.

This PR has each session keep the agent's own running total (the **token ledger**), and each checkpoint store what that total grew by since the session's previous checkpoint.

## 1. One shared reader for every agent
`agent.ReadCumulativeUsage` reads a session's running total for any agent. It owns the files:
- it reads only the bytes appended since the last reading (a no-op reading costs under 1ms), and waits for a line's end;
- it detects a rewritten transcript (the 512 bytes before its last offset no longer match) and reads it again, reporting `Restarted`;
- it reads a small or rewritten file (OpenCode's export, Droid's `settings.json`, a Claude Code subagent) whole, only when its size or last bytes changed, and never reports that as a restart;
- it never follows a symlink or opens a FIFO beside the transcript, and reads `.entire` through its confined reader.

Each agent supplies a `UsageCounter` (50–150 lines) built from shared parts in `agent/usage_counting.go`:
- `KeyedUsage` counts per-call records once per key, with the agent's rule for a repeated record (`KeepFirst` for replays, `KeepLast` for records re-written, `KeepMostOutput` for streamed messages), a window of open records per file, and per-child sums;
- `RunningTotal` sums running totals across a counter restart; `KeyedUsage.CoveredBy` combines records with a running total where an agent writes both.

| Agent | What it counts |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | Assistant messages by `message.id`, most output winning; subagents (and their subagents, Workflow agents) as children |
| Codex | `token_usage_record` by `response_id` (replays keep the first copy), combined with segment-summed `token_count` totals; children from the session's subagent inventory |
| Copilot CLI | `session.usage_record` by `apiCallId` (cache split out of input), combined with `session.shutdown` totals, which include subagents, so their records are subtracted |
| OpenCode | The export's assistant messages, reasoning counted once |
| Pi | Per-message usage on every branch |
| Factory Droid | `settings.json`'s `tokenUsage`, one call per assistant message |
| Antigravity | `PLANNER_RESPONSE` step usage by step index |

Child sessions (Droid Workers, OpenCode child sessions) are not read here: #2824's child-session credit counts them once, and ledger checkpoints add it as the per-turn path does.

## 2. The token ledger
- `SessionState.TokenLedger` (`session/token_ledger.go`, `strategy/token_ledger.go`) holds the running total, read **under the session lock** at turn start, every Stop and every condensation. `TokenUsage` is its total; a checkpoint stores its pending growth; a successful checkpoint write (or attach) marks it checkpointed, and that mark never moves back.
  - A repeated or concurrent Stop reads the same total, so it adds nothing — including on a turn that changed files.
  - A commit in the middle of a turn stores everything up to the commit; the rest lands in the next checkpoint. A message straddling that commit counts once.
- **Which sessions:** sessions this CLI starts at a turn start, for the seven agents above. Legacy states, states created at Stop or by attach, Cursor, Vogon and external agents keep today's per-turn path unchanged.
- **Takes over at the first reading with usage**; what the per-turn accounting already checkpointed counts as checkpointed.
- **Rewritten transcripts:** a lower reading is ignored (a stale copy), unless the transcript restarted: then the difference moves to `Base` and the total carries on.
- **Stop** skips the per-turn token calculation for ledger sessions (for Claude Code it read every subagent transcript only to be discarded).
- **Session end** takes a last reading, so usage an agent writes after its final Stop (Copilot's shutdown totals) is counted.
- **Attach** reads the transcript being attached, updates session state under the session lock, and marks as checkpointed exactly what its checkpoint stored.
- **Checkpoint metadata** adds `session_token_usage`, the session's running total at that checkpoint, next to `token_usage`.

## Checked
- **Real sessions, old vs new:** 726 local sessions across six agents on the final code (154 Copilot, 302 Codex, 149 Claude Code, 39 Antigravity, 37 Pi, 45 Droid), plus 36 OpenCode exports on an earlier revision: the shared reader gives exactly the totals of the per-agent code it replaces, and reading each file in nine pieces gives the same totals as one read. The only difference is intended: Droid Workers are no longer the ledger's children (13 sessions), because #2824's child-session credit counts them. Worst incremental step 126ms; largest cursor 38KB (a Claude session with 190 subagents: 123KB).
- **Live sessions** (`e2e/tests/token_ledger_test.go`): turns that changed files, one that changed nothing, and an agent commit mid-turn; for every session, checkpoints plus pending equal the session total, which equals a fresh read of the agent's files. Passes for Copilot, OpenCode, Pi, Droid and Antigravity. Codex and Claude Code still need a run with working API keys.

## Tests
- `TestUsageCounters_Conformance`: every agent with a counter needs a fixture in `testdata/usage/<agent>/`, read whole, in pieces cut at and around every line end, and after a rewrite.
- Reader tests: partial lines, rewrites, whole files, symlinked files beside the transcript, files that fail to read and return, moved files, the per-file window, merge policies.
- Ledger unit and strategy tests: repeated readings, growth, stale reads, rewrites, child high-water marks, handover from the per-turn accounting, attach under the lock, adopt's copy.
- Integration through the real hooks: Claude Code (repeated Stop on a file-changing turn, no-change turns between commits, mid-turn agent commit, a message straddling it, a subagent finishing in a later turn, a rewritten transcript), Codex (repeated Stop, mid-turn commit), Droid (Worker plus the parent's second Stop). With the ledger off, the repeated Stop and the straddling message fail.

`mise run lint`: 0 issues. Unit and integration suites pass.

Size: +2772/-30 in total.

## Not in this PR / known limits
- External agents keep the per-turn accounting (the protocol has no incremental token call).
- A session's first reading reads its files whole (1.3s on an 82MB Claude transcript with 190 subagents); every later reading reads what was appended. Codex children are still read through the inventory on each reading.
- Only an appended transcript can report a rewrite; for an OpenCode undo, or a Droid rewrite, a lower total is ignored until the total passes the old one — an undercount, not a double count.
- A crash between a checkpoint write and the state save can store the same growth twice (true of main's accounting too).
- A session whose state was lost counts from its next turn start; seeding from the latest checkpoint's `session_token_usage` is a follow-up. Deleting the per-turn path once legacy states age out, and server use of `session_token_usage`, are follow-ups.
- Overlaps #2856 (mid-turn double count): for ledger sessions it is superseded; whichever lands second reconciles.

`SanitizePathForCursor` builds the name of Cursor's project directory (`~/.cursor/projects/<name>`) from the repo path, but not the way Cursor does. Cursor collapses runs of non-alphanumeric characters into one `-` and trims `-` from both ends; Entire only stripped the leading `/` and replaced each character separately. Any path with two separators in a row (a `.worktrees` checkout, `/-…` segments) or any Windows path (`C:\…` → `C--…`) got a directory Cursor never writes to.

Everything Entire computes from that directory is then wrong: resume restores a transcript where Cursor never reads it, attach and history import look in the wrong place, transcript discovery misses the session, and a transcript under Cursor's real directory isn't recognised as Cursor's. Cursor's hooks send `transcript_path: null` until the transcript file exists, so on a session's first turn the turn start computes the path, and the wrong one stays in session state until the next hook carries the real path.

On this machine, Entire's rule names 60 of the 78 Cursor project directories correctly (from their `.workspace-trusted` files); all 18 misses are worktrees or `--` paths. Windows paths are affected too (`C:\repo` → `C--repo`, Cursor uses `C-repo`).

## Change

- `SanitizePathForCursor` now matches Cursor's rule exactly, taken from cursor-agent's `workspace-paths.js` (2026.10.22; the IDE ships the same function): `t.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g,"-").replace(/-+/g,"-").replace(/^-+|-+$/g,"")`. ASCII-only, case kept. It matches all 78 directories on this machine.
- History import's repo-boundary walk (`pathsWithEncoding`, which refuses transcripts whose project directory another repo also maps to) assumed one output character per path character. With collapsing and trimming, a directory can encode to nothing or to the target itself and still lead to a match, so the walk now descends into those too. It stays fail-closed: if the walk hits its read limit, the transcript is treated as shared and not imported.
- Comments that said "the CLI sends a null transcript_path" now say it's null until the transcript exists, in both the IDE and the CLI.

No fallback to the old naming: Cursor never wrote under it, so nothing on disk depends on it. Resume now writes into the directory Cursor actually reads (still guarded by the existing-log check and `--force`).

## Tests

- Sanitizer table with collapsing, trimming, Windows, worktree and case rows; a parity table whose expected values come from running Cursor's own function (empty, `/`, `-`, `/a/`, non-ASCII letters, emoji, NUL, `C:\x`, `C:/x`).
- `GetSessionDir` for a `.worktrees` repo with a temp `HOME`.
- First turn: a repo under `<tmp>/a/.worktrees/repo`, the transcript where Cursor writes it, and a `stop` with `transcript_path: null` resolves to that file.
- Import walk: checked against a brute-force enumeration of a small tree, and a collision that only exists under Cursor's rule (`x/.wt/r` vs `x/wt/r`).
- Import walk: the volume root is a candidate too (`/` encodes like `/---` under the new rule).
- All new tests fail on main; the walk test also fails with the new rule and the old walk.
- **Live, cursor-agent 2026.10.22 (Auto → Claude Haiku), a repo under `…/proj/.worktrees/repo`, three turns and a commit:** on main the first turn start computed `…-proj--worktrees-repo` while Cursor wrote to `…-proj-worktrees-repo`; with this change Entire computes Cursor's directory. On this version the stop hook already carries the real `transcript_path` on the first turn, so turn 1 was recorded on both builds; with this change the session's token totals equal the sum of Cursor's stop-hook usage exactly. An earlier live session (Oct 19, older setup) lost its first checkpoint to this mismatch; that wasn't reproduced on the current CLI.
- The existing Cursor integration tests set `ENTIRE_TEST_CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR`, which bypasses the sanitizer; that's why CI never caught this.

## Not in this PR

- A session started before upgrading that never gets another turn keeps its old stored path.
- A workspace opened through a symlinked path (`/tmp` vs `/private/tmp`) still differs from the git root Entire uses; Cursor names the directory after the path as opened.

## Problem

Entire tracks Antigravity (agy) subagents as unrelated top-level sessions and counts agy's tokens from the wrong source. A live run on main (agy 1.4.2, one subagent):

| | Entire on main | agy's own per-call records |
|---|---|---|
| Parent session | 16,478 in / 134 out, 2 calls | 81,107 / 926, 10 calls |
| Subagent | 0 | 18,519 / 254, 3 calls |
| Plain session, 4 turns | 95 / 27 | 48,383 / 98 |

The causes:

- **Wrong token source.** Entire reads agy's tokens only from the title/statusline feed, which has three problems:
  - the snapshot carrying a turn's last call usually lands just after Stop, so single-call turns record nothing;
  - its `total_input_tokens` is how full the context is, not a running total;
  - it never fires for subagent conversations or `agy -p`.
- **Subagents aren't linked to their parent.** agy runs each `invoke_subagent` as a separate conversation with its own hooks, and Entire records it as a separate top-level session.
- **Parent turns restart mid-turn.** A parent waiting on a subagent is resumed by a new execution whose first PreInvocation has `invocationNum` 0. That fired an unconditional TurnStart, so everything before the last resume dropped out of the turn.
- **Parent turns can stay open forever.** If the parent's last Stop (`fullyIdle: false`) lands before the subagent finishes, agy sends the parent nothing further. Its turn never ends, and in `-p` mode the parent stays ACTIVE as a ghost.

## Change

1. **Tokens from the transcript.** Since 1.4, agy writes each model call's `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and `cache_read_tokens` on its `PLANNER_RESPONSE` step in `transcript_full.jsonl`.
   - Antigravity now implements `TokenCalculator` over those steps, so `resolveTurnTokenUsage` reads them before the statusline.
   - `output_tokens` already includes reasoning: in print mode agy reports `thinking_tokens` 2310 inside `output_tokens` 2313.
   - Transcripts without these fields (older agy) return nil, so the statusline stays the fallback for them.
2. **Subagent support.** Antigravity implements `SubagentSessionResolver`, the interface Factory Droid Workers use.
   - The link needs two text formats agy writes, and both must be present:
     - the child transcript's first step is a `SYSTEM_MESSAGE` with `sender=<parent>`;
     - the parent's transcript has a "Created the following subagent" step naming the child.
   - The task's tool-use ID is the child's conversation ID, since agy tool calls have no IDs. Its type and description come from the call's `TypeName` and `Role`.
   - If agy changes either format, the child falls back to being a top-level session, as on main.
3. **Subagent sessions never act on their own** (shared code, so Droid Workers get this too).
   - Once its parent is known, a subagent's state carries `ParentSessionID`. Such a session never links a commit, never condenses on its own, and is never picked as "the calling session". Identity matching would otherwise tie it with the parent, because they share an agy process.
   - Its file changes go to the parent.
   - A live task record on the parent carries its transcript so far, so a commit made while the subagent runs goes to the parent's checkpoint as the parent's task.
   - Condensing a subagent session from doctor or the exited-owner sweep hands its files to the parent and marks it done.
   - Later hooks rebuild the link from the parent's task record instead of re-reading transcripts.
4. **A wake-up doesn't restart the parent's turn.** At PreInvocation, a new prompt's `USER_INPUT` step is already in the transcript, while a subagent's reply isn't yet. So `invocationNum` 0 starts a turn unconditionally only when the transcript ends with `USER_INPUT`, or doesn't exist yet. An Esc-interrupted turn fires no Stop at all, and the next prompt still starts its own turn.
5. **A paused parent is ended when its subagents finish.**
   - A `fullyIdle: false` Stop records the pause (`AwaitingSubagentsAt`), and a resume clears it.
   - The parent's turn is ended only once every subagent the turn involved (launched, messaged, or heard from, per the parent's transcript) has stopped, and every reply it sent (`send_message` to the parent) is in the parent's transcript. An unread reply will wake the parent, so its turn isn't over yet.
   - A subagent whose agent died counts as stopped. A subagent woken again is running.
   - "Done" comes from the subagents' own sessions, not task records, which track pending checkpoint work.
   - The subagent's turn end and the parent's Stop can land milliseconds apart in either order, so both check. The first to find the turn done claims it (`SubagentTurnEndClaimed`, cleared at the next turn start). A pause reported after the claim can't re-arm it.
   - New agent capability: `SubagentReplyCounter`.
6. **Marking at any tool call.** A subagent is marked at its first tool call of any kind, not only at file edits, because a shell command can edit and commit.

## Subagent tokens in the parent's total

Since #2824, an agy child's turns are credited to the parent's total once, on the same path as Factory Droid Workers: `entire status` and the checkpoint's `subagent_tokens` include them. `TestAntigravity_SubagentWorkBelongsToTheParent` checks it.

## Review fixes

- A Stop for a turn already ended for its subagents is dropped, so the parent's tokens and step are not counted twice (`TestAntigravity_LateStopAfterSubagentTurnEndCountsNothing`).
- A working subagent's hooks keep it live, so one running past `StuckActiveThreshold` still holds its parent's turn (`TestAntigravity_LongRunningSubagentKeepsItsParentWaiting`).

### Environment

- Windows 11, build 26300, amd64; Git for Windows and Windows Terminal

### How we reached the cause

1. Inspected the installed hooks and executable paths. A read-only `entire status --json` reproduction avoided fake hook/session events or changes to project contents.
2. Launched the actual Entire executable, bypassing the package-manager shim, with `UseShellExecute=false`, `CreateNoWindow=true` and redirected standard handles. The command returned valid JSON and exit 0, but a desktop observer recorded visible terminal windows, including a Git console.
3. Tried a PowerShell `-WindowStyle Hidden` launch. It did not eliminate the visible windows. One earlier attempt overlapped another job; we did not treat all its windows as Entire's.
4. Read the Codex runner and Entire source. Codex already hides the hook shell. We then recorded process IDs and parent IDs as well as window visibility to identify the descendant responsible.
5. The attributed baseline showed this chain:
   ```text
   Entire status (36248)
     Entire background worker (42740)
       git.exe (8476)  -> conhost.exe (23204)
       git.exe (27384) -> conhost.exe (42148)
       git.exe (34052) -> conhost.exe (28504)
   ```

   ```text

   grandchild allocated a console window: console-window=5710638
   ```

### Cause and proposed correction

`execx.SpawnDetached` currently uses `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | DETACHED_PROCESS` on Windows. The worker therefore has no console for its children to inherit. An ordinary Git subprocess can allocate a new visible console.

The patch gives **background workers** `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | CREATE_NO_WINDOW` instead: they retain a headless console that their descendants inherit. It deliberately preserves `execx.NonInteractive`'s stronger no-console/`CONIN$` behavior. Unix workers still use the existing new-session behavior. Standard handles, environment, process release, signatures, hook commands and agent configuration are unchanged.

This is a narrow worker-launch change, not a blanket replacement of all subprocess calls or a terminal-hiding script. Explicitly interactive commands are not changed.

- After patch: `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/execx -count=1` passed, including the existing tests that protect detached workers from parent-owned pipes.

- The patched CLI returned the same status JSON, exit 0, empty stderr, and **zero visible windows** during an eight-second process/window observation.

```shell

$ claude                                # work as usual
```

Turn splitting, redaction and idempotent checkpoint IDs are reused from agentimport. A one-shot import becomes the same reader started at offset 0.

On nightly `0.11.4-nightly.202610040807.f3f598a47`, a background Claude Code subagent is now captured correctly: the checkpoint stores `tasks/<tool_use_id>/task.json`, the child transcript and the file linkage. That part of #2215 is fixed for this case.

Line attribution is still wrong in one ordinary ordering. If the parent commits in the same turn in which the child finished, the child's lines are attributed to the human. If the parent's turn ends between the child finishing and the commit, attribution is correct.

Nothing errors, and `entire checkpoint explain` does not show attribution, so the fault is only visible in the checkpoint's `metadata.json`.

## Versions

- Entire CLI `0.11.4-nightly.202610040807.f3f598a47` (official `entire_darwin_arm64.tar.gz`, checksum verified), go1.27.1, darwin/arm64
- Claude Code 2.1.289
- Stock hooks from `entire enable --agent claude-code --telemetry=false --skip-push-sessions --absolute-git-hook-path`; `git-refs` checkpoint backend; `manual-commit` strategy; no remote
- Both checkpoints record this nightly as `cli_version`

## Reproduction

1. Create a fresh repository with no remote. Commit one text file.
2. Run `entire enable --agent claude-code` and commit the configuration.
3. Start a fresh Claude Code session in the repository.
4. Ask the parent to launch one ordinary `Agent` child (`general-purpose`, no `run_in_background`) that appends one line to the tracked file. The launch returns `status: "async_launched"`.
5. Have the parent keep working in the same turn while the child runs, for example with other tool calls, so that the completion notification arrives mid-turn.
6. Still in that turn, commit the file.
7. Read `0/metadata.json` from the checkpoint ref.

To see the passing ordering, let the parent end its turn after step 4 and commit after the completion notification starts a new turn.

## Expected

The child's line is attributed to the agent in both orderings: `agent_lines: 1`, `agent_percentage: 100`.

## Actual

Two runs in the same fixture, same binary, same prompt. Each used one child that appended one line to `notes.txt`. Both launches were `async_launched`.

| | Run 1 | Run 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent `stop` hook between child completion and commit | Yes | No |
| Checkpoint | `01M443QWZB119XGHSB6X00VD48` | `01M4443V6VAZS9TVXEMBPKAF70` |
| `task.json`, child transcript, `files: ["notes.txt"]` | Present | Present |
| `initial_attribution.agent_lines` | 1 | 0 |
| `initial_attribution.total_committed` | 1 | 0 |
| `initial_attribution.agent_percentage` | 100 | 0 |
| `prompt_attributions` | `agent_lines_added: 1` | `user_lines_added: 1`, `user_added_per_file: {"notes.txt": 1}` |

In run 2 the parent made two `WebFetch` calls while the child ran. The completion notification was queued and delivered mid-turn, and the commit followed in the same turn.

Log excerpts are from `.entire/logs/entire.log` with `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug`, trimmed to the relevant fields. Times are local (UTC+1).

### Log, run 1 (correct)

```
19:44:56.102 subagent completed  REDACTED agent_id=ab5096f9dc0aee0f3
19:44:56.861 hook invoked  hook=stop

19:45:09.372 post-commit: HandleCondense decision  task_records=1 should_condense=true shadow_branch=entire/8bfb4cc-e3b0c4
19:45:10.051 prompt attribution data  checkpoint=2 user_added=0 agent_added=1
19:45:10.058 attribution calculated  agent_lines=1 human_added=0 total_committed=1 agent_percentage=100 accumulated_user_added=0
```

```
19:51:24.282 subagent completed  REDACTED agent_id=aec7d03cbf26bf858
             (no stop hook before the commit)
19:51:40.778 post-commit: HandleCondense decision  task_records=1 should_condense=true shadow_branch=entire/3130281-e3b0c4
19:51:41.459 attribution: using HEAD as shadow (no shadow branch)
19:51:41.459 prompt attribution data  checkpoint=1 user_added=1 agent_added=0
```

## Likely cause

This is a reading of the logs above, not confirmed in the source.

`subagent-stop` records the task and transcript but does not appear to snapshot the working tree. The shadow branch is only created by the parent's `stop` hook. When the commit lands before any `stop`, attribution falls back to HEAD as the shadow, and the child's edit, which the parent never made through its own tools, is counted as a user change.

At condensation in run 2, Entire already had what it needed: `task_records=1`, and that task's `files` lists `notes.txt`.

## Scope and limits

- One run for each ordering, on macOS arm64 only.
- The two runs used different Claude config directories. The log lines point at the turn boundary, but I have not isolated that variable.
- Not tested: foreground children, read-only children, `SendMessage` continuations, nested agents, or more than one child.
- The parent ending its turn or not while a background child runs is model behaviour, so the same prompt can produce either ordering.

Related: #2215, #2556.

Every Pi subagent run resolves to the same session ID — the literal string
`session` — because the ID is parsed from the transcript's basename, and Pi names
every subagent transcript `session.jsonl`.

Because that ID keys both transcript paths, every subagent run writes over the
previous one, and at commit time the checkpoint reads whichever run happened to
write last:

- **Staged copy:** `captureTranscript` writes `<repo>/.entire/tmp/pi/<id>.json`
  → one `session.json` for all runs.
- **Shadow-branch archive:** `SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID` is
  `.entire/<id>/` → one metadata dir for all runs.
- **Condensation prefers the staged copy** over the shadow archive
  (`strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:1005-1018`), so the wrong content wins
  even where an archive exists.

Net effect: a checkpoint's stored transcript can be a *different subagent's*
conversation. There is no uncontaminated copy to fall back to, because both paths
collapse on the same ID.

Reproduces with one Pi session and one subagent. No concurrency required.

## What is *not* a problem

So this isn't mistaken for an attribution bug: the sessions attached to a commit
are the *correct* ones. A trail shows the Pi parent and the Pi subagent work, both
genuine participants, nothing unrelated. Sessions↔checkpoints is many-to-many and
the subagent session carries the same checkpoint set as its parent, so no
checkpoint linkage is lost.

The damage is to transcript *content*, not to which sessions or checkpoints appear.

## Observed

```
$ entire session list
Pi · gpt-5.6-sol     · session 019fab4c-c147-7b3a-8cc9-9ebd7224663b   turns 3
Pi · claude-sonnet-5 · session session                                turns 9
```

That second row is nine runs across three distinct subagents:

```
~/.pi/agent/sessions/<cwd-slug>/2026-07-29T00-36-01-991Z_019fab4c-…/
  71e7c5e8/run-0/session.jsonl   71e7c5e8/run-1/session.jsonl
  716671d6/run-0/session.jsonl   716671d6/run-1/session.jsonl   716671d6/run-2/session.jsonl
  d93a3451/run-0/session.jsonl   d93a3451/run-1/session.jsonl   d93a3451/run-2/session.jsonl
  d93a3451/run-3/session.jsonl
```

…and a single staged capture for all of them:

```
$ ls -l .entire/tmp/pi/
2075829  019fab4c-c147-7b3a-8cc9-9ebd7224663b.json   ← parent, fine
 197526  session.json                                 ← all 9 runs, last writer wins
```

Two commits were made from this session, at 11:01 and 11:28. `session.json` has an
mtime of 11:26 — so by the time the 11:28 commit condensed, the staged file held
the 11:26 run's transcript, not the run that produced the commit.

## Root cause

Pi writes parent and subagent transcripts in different shapes. The parent's ID is
its filename; a subagent's ID is its *directory* path, and the leaf is named by
role:

```
2026-07-29T00-36-01-991Z_019fab4c-….jsonl                          ← parent: <timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl
2026-07-29T00-36-01-991Z_019fab4c-…/d93a3451/run-0/session.jsonl   ← subagent
```

Refs at `849421758`:

**The ID is derived from the basename.** `agent/pi/lifecycle.go:366-378`:

```go
base := filepath.Base(p)
base = strings.TrimSuffix(base, ".jsonl")
if i := strings.LastIndex(base, "_"); i >= 0 {
    return base[i+1:]
}
return base
```

`…/d93a3451/run-0/session.jsonl` → `session.jsonl` → `session` → no underscore →
returns `session`. The fallback behaves as documented; the problem is that
`filepath.Base` discards the three segments carrying the identity.

**It runs on every event, not just as a fallback.** `lifecycle.go:156-159` only
parses the path when `payload.SessionID` is empty — but
`agent/pi/entire_extension.ts` sends `session_file:` at lines 87, 97 and 120 and
never sends `session_id`. So the parse always runs. The comment at
`lifecycle.go:173` ("Pi emits before_agent_start with a fully-populated session
ID") doesn't hold for the extension the CLI ships.

**Nothing rejects the result.** The only gate is `validation.ValidateSessionID`
(`validation/validators.go:20`), called at the capture choke point
(`lifecycle.go:335`). It checks empty, leading dash, path separators, `.`/`..`,
`:`, and glob metacharacters — "is this safe in a path?", not "is this an
identity?". `session` is a safe path segment and passes. That validator is doing a
different job correctly and shouldn't be extended to cover identity.

**Both transcript paths key on the ID.** Staging at `lifecycle.go:346`:

```go
dst := filepath.Join(dir, sessionID+".json")
```

and the shadow archive via `paths.SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID`:

```go
return EntireMetadataDir + "/" + sessionID
```

**And the staged copy is preferred at read time.**
`strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:1005-1018`, reached from
`extractSessionData` with `liveTranscriptPath = state.TranscriptPath`:

```go
if liveTranscriptPath != "" {
    ...
    if liveData, readErr := os.ReadFile(liveTranscriptPath); readErr == nil && len(liveData) > 0 {
        fullTranscript = string(liveData)
    }
}
if fullTranscript == "" {
    // Fall back to shadow branch copy
```

The documented rationale is sound in general — *"handles the case where SaveStep
was skipped (no code changes) but the transcript continued growing; the shadow
branch copy would be stale"* — i.e. the live file is assumed to be a newer version
of *the same* session. For Pi subagents that assumption inverts: the live file is a
*different subagent's* transcript, so the preference actively selects wrong content.

**Pi subagents never flow through the subagent mechanism.** `lifecycle.go:1088`
derives `SubagentTranscriptPath` from `event.SubagentID`, which is how Claude Code
keeps per-subagent transcripts distinct. Pi's lifecycle events
(`SessionStart`/`TurnStart`/`TurnEnd`/`session_shutdown`) never populate
`SubagentID`, so Pi subagent runs arrive as ordinary turns carrying a colliding
session ID rather than as subagent steps. That's the design-level gap underneath
the parse bug.

## Suggested fix

The identity is already in `payload.SessionFile` — parent UUID plus
`<subagent>/<run>` segments; only `filepath.Base` throws them away. Renaming the
staged capture alone is **not** sufficient, since the shadow archive keys on the
same ID.

Two coherent shapes:

1. **Model Pi subagents as subagents.** Populate `event.SubagentID` from the path
   segments so runs go through the existing `SubagentTranscriptPath` mechanism, and
   let the session ID roll up to the parent UUID. This matches Claude Code, keeps a
   trail's session list to the conversation that drove the work, and gets distinct
   per-run transcripts for free.
2. **Give each run its own session ID** (`019fab4c-…:d93a3451:run-0`). Simpler, but
   it adds session rows that duplicate the parent's checkpoint set.

(1) looks right given the mechanism already exists.

Worth doing alongside either: have `entire_extension.ts` send `session_id`
explicitly so the path parse stops being load-bearing, and add an identity check
distinct from the path-safety one.

## Why tests didn't catch it

`agent/pi/lifecycle_test.go:176` `TestExtractSessionIDFromPath`:

```go
"/tmp/2026-05-09T12-00-00-000Z_abc-123.jsonl": "abc-123",
"abc-123.jsonl":                              "abc-123",
"/tmp/no-underscore-here.jsonl":              "no-underscore-here",   // fallback asserted as correct
"/path/with/multiple_under_scores_id.jsonl":  "id",
```

Every case is a flat file in a sessions directory, and the third pins the fallback
as intended. The nested subagent shape isn't represented, so the model under test
is "Pi transcripts are flat `<timestamp>_<uuid>.jsonl`" — true for parents, false
for subagents.

## Scope

Observed within a single repo. Sessions appear repo-scoped and I have no evidence
of one `session` ID spanning repos — the only other checkout with Pi subagent runs
on disk had no Pi session registered, so that case is untested rather than ruled
out.

## Environment

- Entire CLI 0.9.0 (darwin/arm64, go1.26.4)
- Pi, parent model `gpt-5.6-sol`, subagent model `claude-sonnet-5`

As a less-technical user (Product Manager) who uses Claude Code for rapid prototyping, I frequently spin up quick POCs — creating new repos, committing code, and moving on. I don't follow a traditional developer workflow where I `cd` into a project directory, set up tooling, and then start working. I often create repos on the fly via `gh repo create` or let Claude Code scaffold things directly.

**The problem:** Entire currently requires per-repo configuration (`entire configure` or `entire enable`) before it can track agent sessions. This means any work done in an unconfigured repo is invisible to Entire. For users who move fast and create repos frequently, this is a significant gap — the most interesting agent sessions (the messy, exploratory POC work) are exactly the ones that never get tracked.

## Proposed Behavior

A global configuration mode that automatically enables Entire tracking for **any** git repo where an agent session starts, without requiring per-repo setup first.

Possible implementations:
- **Global agent hooks** installed at the user level (e.g., via `git config --global core.hooksPath` or a Claude Code user-level hook) that detect agent activity and auto-initialize Entire tracking
- **`entire enable --global`** flag that sets a user-level default: "track all repos unless explicitly disabled"
- **Git template directory integration** (`init.templateDir`) so every new `git init` or `git clone` automatically gets Entire hooks
- **Agent-side integration** — Claude Code (and other agents) could check for Entire and auto-configure on session start if global mode is enabled

## Why This Matters

The current per-repo model works well for developers who have a stable set of projects. But for users who:
- Use AI agents as thinking/prototyping tools (not just coding tools)
- Create throwaway repos for POCs, demos, or explorations
- Work across many repos in a single day
- Don't have `entire configure` as part of their muscle memory

...the friction of per-repo setup means Entire misses the very sessions that would benefit most from being tracked. The "commit log for agents" value proposition is strongest when it's **always on**, like how shell history works — you don't configure it per-directory.

## Context

This came up while testing Entire CLI on a new project created during a Claude Code session. The agent created the repo, built the code, committed, and pushed — but because the session was initiated from a different directory, Entire captured zero checkpoints. The work was done, but the "why" behind it was lost.

Related: #985 (global export/viewing across repos) addresses the *read* side of this problem. This issue addresses the *write* side — making sure sessions are captured in the first place.

What's still stale: user-facing docs and a few internal naming references that point users (and contributors reading the code) at the old name.

### Where it's wrong

- **`README.md:435`** — Tells users to set `codex_hooks = true` if configuring Codex manually. Should be `hooks = true`.
- **`cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/AGENT.md:196`** — Describes the feature as `default_enabled: false` (stage: UnderDevelopment). Upstream is now `default_enabled: true`, stage `Stable`, key `hooks`. - **`cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/hooks.go`** — Three internal mentions of `codex_hooks`:
  - Lines 121, 161 — error messages: `"failed to enable codex_hooks feature: %w"`
  - Line 158 — comment: `// Enable the codex_hooks feature in the project-level .codex/config.toml.`

### Evidence from upstream (Codex `main`, latest 0.130.0)

`codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs`:

```rust
    key: "hooks",
```

`codex-rs/features/src/legacy.rs` keeps `codex_hooks` as a deprecated alias that emits a startup warning.

`default_enabled: true` means newer Codex versions don't strictly need the line, but:

- Entire CLI users may be on older Codex builds where the default was still `false`.
- The migration logic in `ensureProjectFeatureEnabled` is idempotent (returns early when `hooks = true` is present).
- Explicit > implicit when documenting which features Entire requires.

Ready for review. #3014 is newly filed and maintainer agreement on the approach is pending. The four full-suite failures below also reproduce on untouched current upstream; this PR does not claim a green full check.

## Reproduction

The standalone test in #3014 uses real checkpoint writers, the generation-aware queue and a local bare remote. I ran the same test against untouched `955fc9ede` and this implementation, with race detection:

| | Published session IDs | Push / queue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upstream `955fc9ede` | `shared-session`, `local-added-session` | Success; queue cleared |
| This PR | `shared-session`, `remote-added-session`, `local-added-session` | Success; queue cleared |

The remote's earlier commit remains an ancestor in both cases. The bug is missing content in the current checkpoint tree, rather than deletion of every older Git object. No live agent or hosted service is needed to reproduce it.

## Implementation

- Compare each replayed change against its original parent instead of blindly replacing tree entries. Incompatible changes stop before the recovered ref is installed and retain the queued generation.
- At checkpoint roots, match sessions by stable session ID. Keep remote order, append independent local sessions, update their file pointers and rebuild totals through the normal writer helpers. Retain the complete session trees, including transcripts, prompts and assets.
- Preserve independent metadata fields, unknown values, JSON number precision, file modes, review flags and commit links. The root branch label stays with the published checkpoint; each session keeps its own branch. Transcripts remain opaque blobs.
- Recognize an already-delivered linear commit sequence by its combined tree change. This lets a stale peer retain a finalized transcript while publishing new independent work.
- Exclude the intentionally deleted checkpoint from local replay during deletion reconciliation; keep unrelated work and the existing compare-and-swap rule.

The checkpoint schema and push-generation/CAS machinery are unchanged. The new merge code reuses the existing tree writer, subtree-removal, path validation, aggregation and JSON helpers.

## Review guide

`checkpoint/replay.go` handles tree-entry conflicts. `replay_sessions.go` handles session identity, paths and aggregates; `replay_json.go` handles metadata fields. `strategy/metadata_reconcile.go` connects replay and recognizes already-delivered sequences. The deletion caller supplies the existing subtree-removal helper.

The commits separate code/regression tests from the updated implementation contracts.

- The original content-loss reproduction fails on current upstream and passes here.
- Regression coverage includes both `git-refs` and `git-branch`, connected/disconnected histories, backfills after reindexing, stale-peer retries, genuine conflicts, file modes, unknown fields, large integers, assets and queue retention.

A `checkpoint_remote` that passes the ownership vote but has no URL the CLI can build fell back to the push remote. Pre-push then delivered session checkpoints to the code repository, possibly a public one, that the user had explicitly routed them away from. Today this hits any provider without a known host, e.g. `"provider": "entire"` with a github.com origin.

## Change

- `remote.PushURL` returns `ErrCheckpointRemoteUnroutable` (and no URL) instead of falling back to the push remote. The error says what to do: point `checkpoint_remote` at a github or gitlab repository, or remove it. It does not quote the remote URL; the parse cause is logged instead, so a URL's raw bytes never reach terminal output.
- A push remote whose URL does not parse (bare local path, scp-style URL with no owner) no longer falls back to origin either. The store is derived from origin's transport first, so a self-hosted origin keeps its checkpoints on its own host; otherwise it goes to the provider's host, or is withheld.
- Every push path honors the withhold, and the refs stay queued locally:
  - pre-push skips the checkpoint push and prints `[entire] Checkpoints were not pushed and stay local: …` on every push until the setting is fixed; the user's own `git push` is not blocked;
  - `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs` and the manual `PushCheckpoints` (`entire checkpoint push`) return the error;
  - `flushCheckpointRefs` refuses a withheld store itself, so a new caller cannot reopen the path.
- Read surfaces stop describing the push remote as the destination:
  - `CheckpointPushTarget` returns the error, so `attach` no longer reports "Pushed checkpoint metadata" for a checkpoint that went nowhere;
  - `status` reports checkpoints as not syncing;
  - remote topology treats the remote as pinned.

Unchanged: inherited (refused) stores still go to the push remote by design. Self-hosted origins still derive a URL on their own host for any provider. Reads are untouched.

## Notes

- Two existing tests pinned the old fallback and are flipped: a `TestPushURL` case (from 1238aff1e2, which fixed the same misroute for github/gitlab and left unknown providers on it), and `TestCheckpointClaimReport`'s unparseable-transport case, which now expects the dedicated store.
- `entire enable` now errors for such a config instead of passing silently.
- The withhold tests push to a reachable bare repository with a queued checkpoint ref and assert nothing lands there. Each was mutation-checked: reverting the `PushURL` fix delivers the ref and fails the test.
- Not covered: Git's own `push --all`/`--mirror`/explicit refspecs can still carry checkpoint refs in the outer push. That predates this change; main's `CheckOuterPushHeldCheckpoints` is the natural place to extend for a follow-up.
- `doctor migrate-checkpoints --remote <url>` still pushes to the URL given. That is the user naming the destination for one command, like an explicit `git push <url>`; the withhold covers the configured store.

This is step 1 toward supporting `entire` as a `checkpoint_remote` provider (Entire-native `entire://<cluster>/et/<project>/<repo>`). The remaining work (cluster resolution, flag/claim parsing, token handling, ownership vote) is out of scope here.

## Testing

Unit, integration and the Vogon canary pass locally, as do lint and `GOOS=windows go vet`. Two local-only exceptions: `TestOpenCodeSeedRepoPlantsDeps` fails with OpenCode 2 installed (CI doesn't run it), and `TestHTTPS_PushFailsWithoutToken/git-refs` hangs on this machine on the base commit too.
